findings.title: UPDATE statement missing WHERE clause updates all tokens
findings.description: The SQL `UPDATE tokens SET expires_at = ?` has no WHERE clause, so calling refresh_token extends the expiry of every session token in the table, not just the one being refreshed. This lets any authenticated user's refresh silently extend every other user's session as well, and in a busy system it effectively disables session expiry for all users. The query should include `WHERE token = ?` (or equivalent) bound to the token being refreshed.

findings.title: Refresh does not rotate the token
findings.description: refresh_token extends the lifetime of the existing token value instead of issuing a new one. Sliding-expiry refresh endpoints are typically expected to rotate the token so a leaked/stolen token has a bounded useful lifetime; returning the same token indefinitely extends the window of exposure for a compromised token.

findings.title: Test does not verify expiry is actually extended or scoped correctly
findings.description: test_refresh_token only asserts that the returned token equals the input; it never checks that expires_at was updated in the database, and it never verifies that refreshing one user's token does not affect other users' tokens. This test would pass even with the missing-WHERE-clause bug above, so it fails to catch the critical defect it should be guarding against.
